claim: Sox2 expressing (sox2+) progenitors in adult mammalian inner ear lose the capacity to regenerate.
source: The sox2 expressing (sox2+) progenitors in adult mammalian inner ear lose the capacity to regenerate while progenitors in the zebrafish lateral line are able to proliferate and regenerate damaged HCs throughout lifetime.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established context for the study.

claim: Progenitors in the zebrafish lateral line are able to proliferate and regenerate damaged HCs throughout lifetime.
source: The sox2 expressing (sox2+) progenitors in adult mammalian inner ear lose the capacity to regenerate while progenitors in the zebrafish lateral line are able to proliferate and regenerate damaged HCs throughout lifetime.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established context, supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: Atoh1a expressing (atoh1a+) HC precursors were the main population that survived post severe injury.
source: The atoh1a expressing (atoh1a+) HC precursors were the main population that survived post severe injury, and gained sox2 expression to initiate progenitor regeneration.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 2C showing atoh1a+ cells surviving post LY+neo treatment.

claim: Atoh1a+ HC precursors gained sox2 expression to initiate progenitor regeneration.
source: The atoh1a expressing (atoh1a+) HC precursors were the main population that survived post severe injury, and gained sox2 expression to initiate progenitor regeneration.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figures 5A-D showing increased atoh1a+sox2+ cells post severe injury.

claim: Yap was activated to upregulate lin28a transcription in response to severe injury.
source: In response to severe injury, yap was activated to upregulate lin28a transcription.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by western blot data in Figure 2G and CHIP-PCR data in Figure 2H showing yap binds lin28a promoter.

claim: Severe-injury-induced progenitor regeneration was disabled in lin28a mutants.
source: Severe-injury-induced progenitor regeneration was disabled in lin28a or yap mutants.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 3 showing reduced proliferation and progenitor recovery in lin28a mutants.

claim: Severe-injury-induced progenitor regeneration was disabled in yap mutants.
source: Severe-injury-induced progenitor regeneration was disabled in lin28a or yap mutants.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 3F showing reduced proliferation in yap mutants.

claim: Overexpression of lin28a initiated the recovery of sox2+ progenitors.
source: In contrary, overexpression of lin28a initiated the recovery of sox2+ progenitors.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figures 4E-F showing increased sox2+ progenitors in hs:lin28a.

claim: MicroRNA let7 acted downstream of lin28a to activate Wnt pathway for promoting regeneration.
source: Mechanistically, microRNA let7 acted downstream of lin28a to activate Wnt pathway for promoting regeneration.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 6 showing let7 overexpression blocks lin28a-induced proliferation and Wnt activation.

claim: During early development of mouse cochlea, the transcription factor sox2 is required to determine the prosensory region that mainly contains progenitors.
source: During early development of mouse cochlea, the transcription factor sox2 is required to determine the prosensory region that mainly contains progenitors (Julian et al., 2013; Kiernan et al., 2005; Dabdoub et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by three citations to previous studies.

claim: From E12.5 to E14.5 sox2+ progenitors exit cell cycle and differentiate into auditory HCs and SCs.
source: From E12.5 to E14.5 sox2+ progenitors exit cell cycle and differentiate into auditory HCs and SCs.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about mouse cochlear development.

claim: Atoh1 deficiency causes complete loss of cochlear HCs.
source: Basic helix-loop-helix (bHLH) transcription factor atoh1 acts as the cardinal gene initiating auditory HC differentiation since atoh1 deficiency causes complete loss of cochlear HCs (Bermingham et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Bermingham et al., 1999.

claim: A subset of post-mitotic progenitors start to express high levels of atoh1 and downregulate sox2 expression to differentiate into the HC precursors.
source: A subset of post-mitotic progenitors start to express high levels of atoh1 and downregulate sox2 expression to differentiate into the HC precursors (Dabdoub et al., 2008; Zhong et al., 2019; Cai and Groves, 2015; Zhang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by four citations to previous studies.

claim: Terminal differentiation toward mature HCs is promoted by the upregulation of atoh1 target genes, such as pou4f3.
source: Afterwards, their terminal differentiation toward mature HCs is promoted by the upregulation of atoh1 target genes, such as pou4f3 (Cai et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Cai et al., 2015.

claim: Differentiating HCs secret Notch ligands to activate Notch pathway, which inhibits atoh1 expression in neighboring cells and forces them to adopt the SC fate.
source: In the meanwhile, differentiating HCs secret Notch ligands to activate Notch pathway, which inhibits atoh1 expression in neighboring cells and forces them to adopt the SC fate (Abdolazimi et al., 2016; Costa et al., 2017; Lanford et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by three citations to previous studies.

claim: The zebrafish lateral line is a mechanosensory organ composed of a series of neuromasts distributed on the body surface for detecting water flow.
source: The zebrafish lateral line is a mechanosensory organ composed of a series of neuromasts distributed on the body surface for detecting water flow.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about zebrafish lateral line anatomy.

claim: The lateral line HCs share similarities with their counterparts in mammalian inner ear in morphology, function and developmental pathways.
source: The lateral line HCs share similarities with their counterparts in mammalian inner ear in morphology, function and developmental pathways (Whitfield, 2002; Nicolson, 2005).
evidence: This is supported by two citations to previous studies.

claim: Each neuromast contains sensory HCs in the center surrounded by SCs and mantle cells (MCs).
source: Each neuromast contains sensory HCs in the center surrounded by SCs and mantle cells (MCs).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about neuromast structure.

claim: Aminoglycoside antibiotics, such as neomycin, ablates mature HCs and initiates robust mitotic regeneration that is characterized with SC division and differentiation.
source: Aminoglycoside antibiotics, such as neomycin, ablates mature HCs and initiates robust mitotic regeneration that is characterized with SC division and differentiation (Harris et al., 2003; Jiang et al., 2014; Williams and Holder, 2000; Ma et al., 2008; Romero-Carvajal et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by five citations to previous studies.

claim: The powerful capacity to regenerate HCs sustains after multiple rounds of damage, and retains throughout lifetime.
source: The powerful capacity to regenerate HCs sustains after multiple rounds of damage, and retains throughout lifetime (Cruz et al., 2015; Pinto-Teixeira et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by two citations to previous studies.

claim: After severe loss of the tissue integrity, the residual SCs have high potential to recover the neuromast by acting plastic to generate all three cell types.
source: Even after severe loss of the tissue integrity, the residual SCs have high potential to recover the neuromast by acting plastic to generate all three cell types (Viader-Llargués et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Viader-Llargués et al., 2018.

claim: Atoh1a is expressed in HC precursors but not mature HCs in neuromast.
source: Like in inner ear, atoh1a is expressed in HC precursors but not mature HCs in neuromast while sox2 is expressed in a part of SCs and MCs (Ma et al., 2008; Lush et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by two citations to previous studies.

claim: Sox2 is expressed in a part of SCs and MCs in neuromast.
source: Like in inner ear, atoh1a is expressed in HC precursors but not mature HCs in neuromast while sox2 is expressed in a part of SCs and MCs (Ma et al., 2008; Lush et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by two citations to previous studies.

claim: Sox2+ SCs behave as progenitors to proliferate and differentiate through activation of canonical Wnt pathway during regeneration.
source: Sox2+ SCs behave as progenitors to proliferate and differentiate through activation of canonical Wnt pathway during regeneration (Hernández et al., 2007; Jacques et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by two citations to previous studies.

claim: Mammalian sensory HCs are vulnerable to damages caused by antibiotics, chemotherapeutical drugs and noise, which results in various hearing and balance diseases.
source: Mammalian sensory HCs are vulnerable to damages caused by antibiotics, chemotherapeutical drugs and noise, which results in various hearing and balance diseases (Cox et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Cox et al., 2014.

claim: The principal method used to initiate auditory HC regeneration in mammalian inner ear is to induce the transdifferentiation of SCs into HCs by upregulating atoh1 expression.
source: Until now, the principal method used to initiate auditory HC regeneration in mammalian inner ear is to induce the transdifferentiation of SCs into HCs by upregulating atoh1 expression.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about current approaches to HC regeneration.

claim: Many studies tried to overexpress atoh1 in SCs with adenovirus, or used Notch inhibitor to increase atoh1 expression.
source: For example, many studies tried to overexpress atoh1 in SCs with adenovirus, or used Notch inhibitor to increase atoh1 expression (Atkinson et al., 2018; Mizutari et al., 2013; Izumikawa et al., 2005; Yang et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by four citations to previous studies.

claim: The efficiency of HC induction is very low and SCs are lost due to transdifferentiation, resulting in very limited progress toward hearing recovery.
source: However, because the efficiency of HC induction is very low and SCs are lost due to transdifferentiation, very limited progress toward hearing recovery has been achieved (Cox et al., 2014; Zheng and Zuo, 2017; Chen et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by three citations to previous studies.

claim: Using the γ-secretase inhibitor LY411575 to inhibit Notch pathway from 3-day-post-fertilization (dpf) to 5dpf, SCs were exhausted by persistent differentiation into HCs.
source: Using the γ-secretase inhibitor LY411575 to inhibit Notch pathway from 3-day-post-fertilization (dpf) to 5dpf, we found that SCs were exhausted by persistent differentiation into HCs (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The number of sox2+ cells was not changed post neomycin treatment alone.
source: While the distribution of sox2+ cells moved to the center post neo compared with normal larvae, the number was not changed.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by data in Figure 1A-B showing no significant change in sox2+ cell number post neo.

claim: Sox2+ cell number was dramatically decreased after LY or LY+neo treatment.
source: But sox2+ cell number was dramatically decreased after LY or LY+neo (Figure 1A–B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by data in Figure 1A-B showing significant reduction in sox2+ cells.

claim: Sox2+ progenitors were able to recover quickly post LY+neo, with a few appearing at 6 hr and recovering to normal level by 48 hr.
source: Surprisingly, sox2+ progenitors were able to recover quickly post LY+neo. A few sox2+ progenitors appeared early at 6 hr, with increased sox2+ progenitors being regenerated afterwards and recovered to normal level by 48 hr.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by data in Figure 1A-B showing time course of sox2+ progenitor recovery.

claim: ET4+ HCs appeared at 48 hr post LY+neo, suggesting that HC regeneration happened after the recovery of sox2+ progenitors.
source: In Figure 1A, ET4+ HCs appeared at 48 hr post LY+neo, suggesting that HC regeneration happened after the recovery of sox2+ progenitors.
evidence: This is an inference based on the temporal sequence of events observed in Figure 1A.

claim: The exhausted sox2+ progenitors were not recovered without severe injury (LY+rest condition).
source: In contrast, the exhausted sox2+ progenitors were not recovered without severe injury (Figure 1C–D).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by data in Figure 1C-D comparing LY+rest with LY+neo.

claim: Proliferation in SCs or MCs post severe injury is highly increased compared with neo-induced normal injury, while HC differentiation is decreased.
source: Our results showed that proliferation in SCs or MCs post severe injury is highly increased compared with neo-induced normal injury, while HC differentiation is decreased (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by EdU incorporation data in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Twelve times of MC or SC divisions were recorded in one neuromast from 24 hr to 40 hr post LY+neo, but none of them was differentiation.
source: By time lapse, we recorded 12 times of MC or SC divisions in one neuromast from 24 hr to 40 hr post LY+neo, but none of them was differentiation (Video 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by time-lapse imaging data in Video 1.

claim: Lin28a was transiently upregulated post neomycin treatment according to RNA-Seq analysis.
source: Previously, we have collected samples of regenerating neuromasts for RNA-Seq analysis (Jiang et al., 2014) and identified that lin28a was transiently upregulated post neomycin treatment (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by RNA-Seq data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Lin28a was not expressed in the developing lateral line primordium or neuromast.
source: By in situ hybridization, we verified that lin28a was not expressed in the developing lateral line primordium or neuromast (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by in situ hybridization data in Figure 2A.

claim: Neomycin treatment and other types of HC injuries, including heavy metal (copper sulfate) or chemotherapeutic drug (cisplatin), induced sporadic lin28a expression.
source: Neomycin treatment and other types of HC injuries, including heavy metal (copper sulfate) or chemotherapeutic drug (cisplatin), induced sporadic lin28a expression (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by in situ hybridization data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: LY+neo induced much higher expression of lin28a compared with neo alone.
source: Interestingly, LY+neo induced much higher expression of lin28a compared with neo alone (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by in situ hybridization data in Figure 2B.

claim: Lin28a induction is proportional to the injury size.
source: Since LY+neo induced more cell death than neo as illustrated by ablation of s100t expressing HCs, we tested whether lin28a induction is proportional to the injury size.
evidence: This is tested by laser ablation experiments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C-D.

claim: Low level of lin28a was induced when five HCs were ablated while higher level of lin28a was observed when sixteen HCs were ablated.
source: We used laser ablation to manipulate the number of injured cells in LY-treated neuromast. Low level of lin28a was induced when five HCs were ablated while higher level of lin28a was observed when sixteen HCs were ablated.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by laser ablation data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The ablation of SCs could also induce lin28a expression.
source: Furthermore, we found that the ablation of SCs could also induce lin28a expression (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C–D).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by laser ablation data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The number of atoh1a-transcribed cells detected by in situ were higher at 1 hr post LY+neo compared with LY.
source: We noticed that atoh1a+HC precursors were the main population that survived post LY+neo (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by in situ hybridization data in Figure 2C.

claim: Lin28a was co-expressed with atoh1a post neo or LY+neo.
source: Using double fluorescent in situ, it was verified that lin28a was induced in atoh1a+ HC precursors in both neo- and LY+neo-treated neuromasts (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by double fluorescent in situ data in Figure 2D.

claim: Neo-induced lin28a was increased when atoh1a was overexpressed in hs:atoh1a.
source: We used hs:atoh1a to induce atoh1a expression after heat shock and found that neo-induced lin28a was increased (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by in situ hybridization data in Figure 2E.

claim: Lin28a induction post LY+neo was completely blocked when atoh1a expression was inhibited in hs:notch1a.
source: In contrast, lin28a induction post LY+neo was completely blocked when atoh1a expression was inhibited in hs:notch1a (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by in situ hybridization data in Figure 2F.

claim: Wnt activation does not act upstream to induce lin28a expression post injury.
source: We used hs:dkk1 to inhibit Wnt activation and found that lin28a induction post injury was not affected (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by in situ hybridization data in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A.

claim: The protein levels of yap was up-regulated at 1 hr post LY+neo while taz was increased until 5 hr.
source: We found the protein levels of yap was up-regulated at 1 hr post LY+neo while taz was increased until 5 hr (Figure 2G and Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by western blot data in Figure 2G and Figure 2—figure supplement 2B.

claim: More yap was detected in LY+neo-treated neuromast cells compared with neo by immunostaining.
source: By immunostaining, more yap was also dectected in LY+neo-treated neuromast cells compared with neo.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by immunostaining data in Figure 2—figure supplement 2D-E.

claim: Yap expression was inhibited when atoh1a is inhibited with hs:notch1a, suggesting that yap is activated in atoh1a+ HC precursors.
source: Yap expression was inhibited when atoh1a is inhibited with hs:notch1a, which suggests that yap is activated in atoh1a+ HC precursors (Figure 2—figure supplement 2D–G).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by immunostaining data in Figure 2—figure supplement 2G, with inference about cell type.

claim: Expressions of the classic yap target genes, such as cyr61 and ctgfa, and the Hippo pathway genes, such as yap and mst2, were dramatically increased post LY+neo.
source: Expressions of the classic yap target genes, such as cyr61 and ctgfa, and the Hippo pathway genes, such as yap and mst2, were dramatically increased post LY+neo (Figure 2—figure supplement 2H–I), which was blocked with verteporfin (an inhibitor of yap-mediated transcription by blocking yap-tead1 interaction).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by qPCR data in Figure 2—figure supplement 2H-I.

claim: A conserved yap binding motif is located at 100 bp downstream of lin28a transcription start site, where a tead1 binding motif is located nearby.
source: Interesting we found a conserved yap binding motif located at 100 bp downstream of lin28a transcription start site, where a tead1 binding motif is located nearby.
evidence: This is a finding from bioinformatic analysis shown in Figure 2H.

claim: Yap directly binds to the predicted region of lin28a promoter post severe injury.
source: We used CHIP-PCR to verify that yap directly binds to this region of lin28a promoter post severe injury (Figure 2H).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by CHIP-PCR data in Figure 2H.

claim: LY+neo-induced lin28a expression was blocked in verteporfin or in yap mutant.
source: In addition, LY+neo-induced lin28a expression was blocked in verteporfin or in yap mutant (Figure 2I–J).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by in situ hybridization data in Figure 2I-J.

claim: Lin28a deficiency had no effect on HC or SC number in homeostasis.
source: We found that lin28a deficiency had no effect on HC or SC number in homeostasis, nor did it affect exhaustion of sox2+ progenitors post LY or LY+neo (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by cell counting data in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Lin28a deficiency did not affect exhaustion of sox2+ progenitors post LY or LY+neo.
source: We found that lin28a deficiency had no effect on HC or SC number in homeostasis, nor did it affect exhaustion of sox2+ progenitors post LY or LY+neo (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by cell counting data in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: The regenerated HC number was decreased by lin28a deficiency post LY+neo.
source: We found that the regenerated HC number was decreased by lin28a deficiency (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by cell counting data in Figure 3A.

claim: The number of regenerated SCs and the proliferative SCs were both significantly decreased in lin28a mutant post LY+neo.
source: In addition, the number of regenerated SCs (Figure 3A) and the proliferative SCs (Figure 3B) were both significantly decreased.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by cell counting and EdU incorporation data in Figure 3A-B.

claim: The EdU-positive SC cells that were located in each quadrant with no polarization in sibling post LY+neo were almost cleared in lin28a mutant.
source: The EdU-positive SC cells that were located in each quadrant with no polarization in sibling post LY+neo were almost cleared in lin28a mutant (Figure 3C–D).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by EdU incorporation and spatial analysis data in Figure 3C-D.

claim: The EdU-positive SC number post neo is not affected by lin28a deficiency.
source: In contrast, the EdU-positive SC number post neo is not affected by lin28a deficiency (Figure 3E), indicating that lin28a is not required for neo-induced regeneration.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by EdU incorporation data in Figure 3E.

claim: Yap deficiency or inhibition with verteporfin caused proliferative deficiency post LY+neo, but has no effect on SC proliferation post neo.
source: We also observed that yap deficiency induced similar phenotype with lin28a mutant. Yap mutation or inhibition with verteporfin caused proliferative deficiency post LY+neo, but has no effect on SC proliferation post neo (Figure 3F–G and data not shown).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by EdU incorporation data in Figure 3F-G.

claim: Proliferative deficiency in verterporfin was rescued by hs:lin28a, indicating that lin28a acts downstream of yap to promote SC proliferation.
source: Proliferative deficiency in verterporfin was rescued by hs:lin28a (Figure 3G), indicating that lin28a acts downstream of yap to promote SC proliferation.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by EdU incorporation data in Figure 3G, with inference about pathway relationship.

claim: The number of proliferative and regenerated progenitors at 12 hr post injury were significantly reduced in lin28a mutant.
source: We next examined whether lin28a is required for recovery of sox2+ progenitors post LY+neo. The number of proliferative and regenerated progenitors at 12 hr post injury were significantly reduced in lin28a mutant (Figure 3H–I).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by immunostaining and EdU incorporation data in Figure 3H-I.

claim: The HC number was not changed in hs:lin28a, indicating that lin28a has no effect on HC development.
source: We found that the HC number was not changed in hs:lin28a, indicating that lin28a has no effect on HC development (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by cell counting data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The number of proliferative SCs was significantly increased when lin28a is overexpressed in both homeostatic and neo-treated neuromast, whereas HC differentiation was not changed.
source: The number of proliferative SCs was significantly increased when lin28a is overexpressed in both homeostatic and neo-treated neuromast, whereas HC differentiation was not changed (Figure 4A–B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by BrdU incorporation data in Figure 4A-B.

claim: The location of proliferative SCs still remain polarized in hs:lin28a.
source: The proliferative SCs are localized in dorsal and ventral poles of neuromast in homeostasis and neo-induced regeneration (Ma et al., 2008; Romero-Carvajal et al., 2015; Wibowo et al., 2011). The location of proliferative SCs still remain polarized in hs:lin28a (Figure 4C–D).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by spatial analysis data in Figure 4C-D.

claim: Lin28a overexpression is sufficient to induce higher number of proliferative progenitors post LY.
source: We further examined whether lin28a overexpression is sufficient to induce sox2+ progenitors, and observed higher number of proliferative progenitors in hs:lin28a post LY (Figure 4E–F).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by immunostaining and EdU incorporation data in Figure 4E-F.

claim: The number of atoh1a+sox2+ cells in LY+neo was significantly increased compared with neo.
source: We co-labeled the expressions of atoh1a mRNA and sox2 protein and found that the number of atoh1a+sox2+ cells in LY+neo was significantly increased compared with neo (Figure 5A–B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by double labeling data in Figure 5A-B.

claim: Very few Tomato+ cells express sox2 in normal or LY-treated larvae.
source: The atoh1a:TdTomato reporter labeled partially ET4-positive HCs (Figue 5C, ctrl) and also a few cells that are ET4 negative and sox2 negative which are likely HC precursors (Figure 5C, yellow arrows in LY). Very few Tomato+ cells express sox2 in normal or LY-treated larvae.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by reporter imaging data in Figure 5C.

claim: Significantly more Tomato+ cells turned on sox2 expression at 12 hr and 48 hr post LY+neo and become Tomato+sox2+ cells.
source: However, significantly more Tomato+ cells turned on sox2 expression at 12 hr and 48 hr post LY+neo and become Tomato+sox2+ cells (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by reporter imaging data in Figure 5D.

claim: Tomato+ cells became HCs in both neo and LY+neo.
source: We further used time-lapse microscopy to trace atoh1a:TdTomato cells and found that the Tomato+ cells became HCs in both neo and LY+neo (blue dots in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–B, Video 2 and S3).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by time-lapse imaging data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A-B and Videos 2-3.

claim: It's only in LY+neo-induced severe injury that Tomato+ cells became sox2-positive cells labeled by sox2:GFP.
source: However, it's only in LY+neo-induced severe injury that Tomato+ cells became sox2-positive cells labeled by sox2:GFP (white dots in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B and Video 3).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by time-lapse imaging data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B and Video 3.

claim: Significantly higher ratio of SCs were labeled by Tomato post LY+neo compared with neo.
source: We traced the Tomato+ cells for their fate becoming HCs, SCs or MCs (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C–D), and the results showed that significantly higher ratio of SCs were labeled by Tomato post LY+neo.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by lineage tracing data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C-D.

claim: Many Tomato+ MCs were labeled post LY+neo, but none was detected in normal or neo-treated larvae, suggesting that atoh1a+sox2+ cells gained more potential to produce MCs.
source: More importantly many Tomato+ MCs were labeled post LY+neo, but none was detected in normal or neo-treated larvae, suggesting that atoh1a+sox2+ cells gained more potential to produce MCs.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by lineage tracing data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C-D, with inference about cell potential.

claim: The Yap inhibitor verteporfin decreased Tomato+sox2+ cell number post severe injury, which was rescued by overexpression of lin28a.
source: We further tested whether HC precursors gained sox2 expression through Yap-lin28a pathway. The Yap inhibitor verteporfin decreased Tomato+sox2+ cell number post severe injury, which was rescued by overexpression of lin28a (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by reporter imaging data in Figure 5E.

claim: Significantly higher number of atoh1a+sox2+ cells were induced in LY-treated hs:lin28a.
source: Significantly higher number of atoh1a+sox2+ cells were induced in LY-treated hs:lin28a (Figure 5F–G).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by double labeling data in Figure 5F-G.

claim: hs:let7 showed the defect of SC proliferation post LY+neo, similar to lin28a mutant.
source: Similar with lin28a mutant, hs:let7 showed the defect of SC proliferation post LY+neo (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by EdU incorporation data in Figure 6A.

claim: Overexpression of let7 inhibited hs:lin28a-induced proliferation, indicating that let7 acts downstream of lin28a to promote regeneration.
source: We further found that overexpression of let7 inhibited hs:lin28a-induced proliferation (Figure 6B), indicating that let7 acts downstream of lin28a to promote regeneration.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by EdU incorporation data in Figure 6B, with inference about pathway relationship.

claim: Lin28a has no effect on Notch and Fgf pathways as her4, a Notch pathway gene, and fgf3, a Fgf pathway gene were not changed in hs:lin28a.
source: Lin28a has no effect on Notch and Fgf pathways as her4, a Notch pathway gene, and fgf3, a Fgf pathway gene were not changed in hs:lin28a (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by in situ hybridization data in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Overexpression of lin28a was sufficient to upregulate Wnt pathway genes wnt10a and mycn, which was inhibited by overexpression of let7.
source: Overexpression of lin28a was sufficient to upregulate Wnt pathway genes wnt10a and mycn, which was inhibited by overexpression of let7 (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by in situ hybridization data in Figure 6C.

claim: Activation of Wnt pathway genes at 1 hr post LY+neo were blocked in lin28a mutant.
source: Activation of Wnt pathway genes at 1 hr post LY+neo were blocked in lin28a mutant (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by in situ hybridization data in Figure 6D.

claim: Lin28a-induced proliferation were inhibited by hs:dkk1 in which Wnt activation is blocked.
source: We further tested the function of Wnt pathway and found that lin28a-induced proliferation were inhibited by hs:dkk1 in which Wnt activation is blocked (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by EdU incorporation data in Figure 6E.

claim: Yap-lin28a pathway functions specifically in severe-injury induced regeneration for promoting progenitor recovery.
source: Therefore, our results identified that Yap-lin28a pathway functions specifically in severe-injury induced regeneration for promoting progenitor recovery (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on multiple experimental findings showing differential effects in severe vs. normal injury.

claim: Wnt pathway was highly activated immediately post severe injury, but was not activated at 1 hr post neo.
source: We found that Wnt pathway was highly activated immediately post severe injury, but was not activated at 1 hr post neo.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by in situ hybridization data in Figure 6D.

claim: Lin28a, together with Oct4, Sox2 and Nanog, can reprogram somatic cells to induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSC) in mouse and human.
source: Since it's well-known that lin28a, together with Oct4, Sox2 and Nanog, can reprogram somatic cells to induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSC) in mouse and human (Yu et al., 2007; Moss and Tang, 2003; Zhang et al., 2016), it may be involved in tissue regeneration through dedifferentiation.
evidence: This is supported by three citations to previous studies.

claim: Lin28a may reprogram HC precursors into sox2+ progenitors.
source: Our results showed that atoh1a+ HC precursors were converted into sox2 expressing cells through Yap-lin28a pathway (Figure 5), suggesting that lin28a may reprogram HC precursors into sox2+ progenitors.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the data in Figure 5.

claim: Atoh1+ secretory cells in intestine are capable to dedifferentiate into lgr5+ stem cells in irradiation-induced severe injury.
source: For example, atoh1+ secretory cells in intestine are capable to dedifferentiate into lgr5+ stem cells in irradiation-induced severe injury (Tetteh et al., 2016; Tomic et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by two citations to previous studies.

claim: In colon, atoh1+ secretory progenitors reprogram to lgr5+ stem cells and form the entire crypts post injury while contributed minimally to other lineages in homeostasis.
source: In colon, atoh1+ secretory progenitors reprogram to lgr5+ stem cells and form the entire crypts post injury while contributed minimally to other lineages in homeostasis (Castillo-Azofeifa et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Castillo-Azofeifa et al., 2019.

claim: The severe-injury-treated neuromast displayed the expression patterns of leading progenitors in early developing primordium.
source: However, the severe-injury-treated neuromast displayed the expression patterns of leading progenitors in early developing primordium, which suggests that lin28a reprograms the differentiated cells into the stem/progenitor cells at early developmental stage.
evidence: This is an inference based on gene expression patterns observed in the study.

claim: Lin28a reprograms the differentiated cells into the stem/progenitor cells at early developmental stage.
source: However, the severe-injury-treated neuromast displayed the expression patterns of leading progenitors in early developing primordium, which suggests that lin28a reprograms the differentiated cells into the stem/progenitor cells at early developmental stage.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on gene expression patterns.

claim: The damage of cell junction adjacent to the injury site might activate yap.
source: It is hypothesized that either injured cells secrete diffusible molecules leading to widespread yap activation, or the damage of cell junction adjacent to the injury site activates yap (Moya and Halder, 2016). We observed lin28a induction after laser ablation of HCs in the restricted areas. Our results showed that the lin28a-expressing cells were very close to the damaged HCs (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C), suggesting that the damage of cell junction might lead to yap-lin28a activation.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on spatial proximity of lin28a-expressing cells to damaged HCs.

claim: The loss of amotl2a post HC injury might result in yap activation.
source: Since cell-junction-associated protein amotl2a has been reported restricting yap activity in the zebrafish lateral line primordium (Agarwala et al., 2015), it is possible that the loss of amotl2a post HC injury might result in yap activation.
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis based on previous findings about amotl2a function.

claim: Lin28b-let7 functions to enhance progenitor proliferation during embryonic inner ear development.
source: It was reported that lin28b-let7 functions to enhance progenitor proliferation during embryonic inner ear development (Golden et al., 2015), but the downstream pathway is still unknown.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Golden et al., 2015.

claim: Lin28a regulates retinal regeneration through let7.
source: Our data showed that lin28a-let7 functions to promote progenitor proliferation during regeneration, which is consistent with the previous finding that lin28a regulates retinal regeneration through let7 (Ramachandran et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Ramachandran et al., 2010.

claim: Hippo pathway critically regulates regeneration of many tissues.
source: Because Hippo pathway critically regulates regeneration of many tissues (Gregorieff et al., 2015; Gregorieff and Wrana, 2017; Moya and Halder, 2016), we therefore tested the expression of yap and taz, two cardinal mediators of Hippo pathway.
evidence: This is supported by three citations to previous studies.

claim: Yap has been described as an important regulator in mediating regeneration.
source: Previous studies have described yap as an important regulator in mediating regeneration (Gregorieff and Wrana, 2017; Moya and Halder, 2016), but the downstream mechanism is unclear.
evidence: This is supported by two citations to previous studies.

claim: The lin28a mutant allele (lin28a^psi37) harbors a deletion of five nucleotides and causes a premature stop codon within the cold shock domain.
source: To determine whether lin28a is required for HC regeneration, we generated a lin28a mutant allele (lin28a^psi37, referred to as lin28a-) that harbors a deletion of five nucleotides and causes a premature stop codon within the cold shock domain (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes the generation and characterization of the lin28a mutant.

claim: HCs were increased while SCs were decreased post LY treatment, indicating that LY induced differentiation of SCs into HCs.
source: ET4;ET20 larvae were treated with 2 μM LY from 3dpf to 5dpf followed by neomycin, and the number of HCs, SCs and MCs were counted before and right after neo treatment. Results showed that HCs were increased while SCs were decreased post LY, indicating that LY induced differentiation of SCs into HCs.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by cell counting data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Numbers of HCs, SCs and MCs were all significantly decreased post LY+neo compared with 5dpf normal larvae.
source: Numbers of HCs, SCs and MCs were all significantly decreased post LY+neo compared with 5dpf normal larvae.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by cell counting data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Differentiation rate in LY+neo was decreased compared with neo.
source: Results showed that differentiation rate (HC+ in B) in LY+neo was decreased compared with neo, while proliferative rates of SCs (SC+ in C) and MCs (MC+ in D) were significantly increased.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by EdU incorporation data in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Proliferative rates of SCs and MCs were significantly increased in LY+neo compared with neo.
source: Results showed that differentiation rate (HC+ in B) in LY+neo was decreased compared with neo, while proliferative rates of SCs (SC+ in C) and MCs (MC+ in D) were significantly increased.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by EdU incorporation data in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: GFP-positive cells in neuromast were mostly co-labeled by sox2 antibody.
source: In addition to sox2 antibody staining, we also used sox2-2a-GFP knock-in reporter (sox2:GFP) (Shin et al., 2014) to observe the recovery of sox2+ progenitors. GFP-positive cells in neuromast, which were mostly co-labeled by sox2 antibody, were significantly decreased in LY, and recovered to normal level at 48 hr post LY+neo.
evidence: This validates the sox2:GFP reporter by showing co-labeling with sox2 antibody.

claim: Levels of lats1 and phosphorylated mob1 were not changed at 1 hr post LY+neo, suggesting yap is activated independent of canonical Hippo pathway.
source: Levels of lats1 and phosphorylated mob1 were not changed at 1 hr, suggesting yap is activated independent of canonical Hippo pathway.
evidence: This is an inference based on western blot data in Figure 2—figure supplement 2B showing no change in Hippo pathway components.

claim: The proliferative SCs are evenly distributed in each quadrant with no polarization post LY+neo.
source: EdU plots show the positions of EdU+ nuclei of 18 neuromasts superimposed on the same plane, and rose diagrams document the angular positions of SC+. The results show that the proliferative SCs are evenly distributed in each quadrant with no polarization post LY+neo.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by spatial analysis data in Figure 3D.

claim: The proliferative SCs are localized in dorsal and ventral poles of neuromast in homeostasis and neo-induced regeneration.
source: The proliferative SCs are localized in dorsal and ventral poles of neuromast in homeostasis and neo-induced regeneration (Ma et al., 2008; Romero-Carvajal et al., 2015; Wibowo et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by three citations to previous studies.
